51618477.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to DYRK2 (unknown origin) assessed as dissociation constant by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.SPR Analysis in Results Section: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) results further proved that curcumin and its analogs A1–A3 had a binding affinity with DYRK2 (Figures 1c,d and S1e,f). The dissociation constant (Kd) values of A1–A3 with DYRK2 were 5.0, 4.7, 7.9, and 14.5 μM, respectively. In addition, in vitro enzyme inhibition assays were performed, and the results showed that A1–A3 and curcumin inhibited DYRK2 with half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) values of 28, 19, 24, and 10 nM, respectively (Figure 1e).
original_paragraph.Figure 1 Caption: Figure 1. Design of small-molecule degraders based on PROTAC. (a) Molecular docking simulation of CUR in complex with DYRK2 (PDB entry 5ZTN). (b) Molecular docking simulation of CUR analog A3 in complex with DYRK2 (PDB entry 5ZTN). (c, d) SPR results of CUR and CUR analog A3 with DYRK2. The unit is μM. (e) Enzyme inhibition assay of CUR and A1–A3 on purified DYRK2 in 20 μM ATP concentrations. (f) Chemical structures of the designed compounds. Quantitative data are represented as the mean ± SEM of three independent replicates.
original_paragraph.SPR Sensorgram Data from Figure 1c and 1: Figure 1c shows SPR sensorgrams for CUR at concentrations of 0.3125, 0.625, 1.25, 2.5, 5, 10, and 20 μM. Figure 1d shows SPR sensorgrams for A3 at concentrations of 0.3125, 0.625, 1.25, 2.5, 5, 10, and 20 μM. The x-axis represents time in seconds (0 to 200 s), and the y-axis represents relative response. The curves show association (increasing response) and dissociation (decreasing response) phases.
original_paragraph.Supporting Information Reference in Text: The SPR assay further confirmed the interaction between DYRK2 and CP134, with a Kd value of 29.7 μM (Figure S2e).
